plain_english_policy: Use private-sector commercial health insurance mechanisms (e.g., regulated markets, subsidies) to increase coverage rather than government-run programs.

effects.rationale: The option explicitly frames expansion via commercial insurance, not public systems.
Commercial reform often relies on employer-based or individual market mechanisms that may disproportionately burden lower-income households (e.g., premiums, deductibles).
Regulated commercial markets imply government oversight of private insurance (e.g., mandates, subsidies) rather than laissez-faire.
